proposals.relationship: Uses Bloch’s account of history’s analytical youth and uncertainty to defend continued methodological self-examination.
proposals.evidence_note: Selected published address associated with delivery in1969, concluding paragraphs and notes54/56/58. The notes cite a1964 English edition of The Historian’s Craft; its pages and the French original were not freshly read. This is a particular methodological resource, not a general Annales lineage.
primary_locators: Address paragraphs beginning It is not inconceivable, Marc Bloch had the audacity, and Unlike the sciences also; notes54,56,58.

proposals.relationship: Uses Kuhn’s account of common scientific paradigms to distinguish historians’ recurrent examination of first principles.
proposals.evidence_note: The published address, paragraph beginning Unlike the sciences also and note57, cites The Structure of Scientific Revolutions(1962),162. Woodward doubts history will gain the same release from methodological questioning; he does not simply adopt a Kuhnian historical model. The cited book remains unread here.
primary_locators: Address paragraph beginning Unlike the sciences also; note57 identifies Kuhn1962,162.

proposals.relationship: Regards White’s charge that historians evade the standards of both art and science as exaggerated and open to reply.
proposals.evidence_note: Woodward’s published address explicitly includes the immediately preceding White quotation among criticisms he considers exaggerated, while warning against professional indifference to criticism. Note32 identifies White’s1966 essay. This narrow reservation does not establish rejection of narrative theory or a freshly read rebuttal of White’s complete argument.
primary_locators: Address paragraphs beginning In short, according to one harsh judgment and Some of these attacks; note32, read with the later paragraph beginning Complacency in these matters.

proposals.relationship: McPherson recalls Woodward commissioning his Oxford History volume, before the assignment changed to the era covered by Battle Cry of Freedom.
proposals.evidence_note: McPherson’s own2000 interview with William R.Ferris describes the initial1865–1900 invitation and his requested move to1848–1865 after another contributor fell ill. Editorial contribution is specified; McPherson retains authorship and initiative. This does not make Woodward responsible for every interpretation in the book.
primary_locators: NEH2000 Interview, Ferris question beginning Your best-known book and McPherson’s two-paragraph answer.

proposals.relationship: Joint conception of the Oxford History of the United States provides a shared editorial project.
proposals.evidence_note: McPherson’s2000 recollection names both as conceiving a multiauthor series modelled on the Oxford History of England. Undirected editorial overlap, without causal priority or a shared interpretation of every subject. The transcript’s Hofstetter spelling is a variant, not a second historian.
primary_locators: NEH2000 Interview, first paragraph of McPherson answer to the Battle Cry origin question.

proposals.relationship: As Foner recounts, defends the Populists’ corporate critique against Hofstadter’s emphasis on conspiracy and cultural hatreds.
proposals.evidence_note: Explicit named scholarly mediation: Foner’s2022 review, paragraphs beginning For decades and It was a book, distinguishes their disagreement from friendship. It also notes Woodward later conceded exaggerating white Populists’ racial egalitarianism. Original exchanges and complete books remain unread; editorial collaboration does not erase this disagreement.
primary_locators: Foner2022, paragraphs beginning For decades, Woodward would defend and It was a book for the1930s.

proposals.relationship: Questions the comparative scope of Foner’s Reconstruction while praising its achievement and correcting any implication that Foner lacked comparative expertise.
proposals.evidence_note: Woodward’s May1988 review urges comparisons with other emancipations; his June correction explicitly credits Foner’s Nothing But Freedom(1983). The criticism concerns the larger book’s scope, not ignorance of comparison. Foner’s books remain unread here; praise, qualification and the correction belong to one bounded critical reception.
primary_locators: Unfinished Business: paragraphs Eric Foner has put together, All of the old schools, and It is true that the American experience; Comparative History: both body paragraphs.

proposals.relationship: Criticizes Woodward’s earlier tendency to portray African Americans as victims rather than historical agents, while valuing his engaged scholarship.
proposals.evidence_note: Foner’s own2022 review contrasts Woodward’s previous writing with later grassroots Reconstruction scholarship and ends by crediting his public achievement. This is a particular historiographical criticism, not dismissal of the whole corpus. Woodward’s original books and Cobb’s complete biography remain unread.
primary_locators: Foner2022, paragraph Beginning in the1960s, new scholarship; concluding paragraphs Woodward died and At its best.

proposals.relationship: As Hannah Tandy documents from Woodward’s1938 letter, Black Reconstruction supplied an acknowledged scholarly debt.
proposals.evidence_note: Explicit named scholarly mediation: Tandy’s2021 History MA thesis,31 and note85, identifies the3April1938 letter and Woodward’s acknowledgment. UMass metadata corroborates the letter and debt, but the scan could not be read. The complete book and letter remain unread; the proposal does not adopt Tandy’s wider Watson interpretation.
primary_locators: Tandy2021, printed31(PDF page46), paragraph beginning A1938 letter and note85; UMass item mums312-b087-i148 metadata.

proposals.relationship: Uses Higham’s history of the profession to document American historians’ recovery of intellectual confidence after1945.
proposals.evidence_note: In the published address associated with1969 delivery, Woodward names Higham’s1965 account and quotes its diagnosis of restored professional self-respect. Notes1/11 credit Higham et al.; Leonard Krieger and Felix Gilbert retain their coauthor credit. The complete1965 book remains unread here; this is a specified historiographical resource, not an exclusive lineage.
primary_locators: Address paragraph beginning They quoted Friedrich Meinecke, concluding sentences beginning By1965 Higham could note; notes1 and11, which cite History(1965),132–137; note5 separately cites135. Coauthor metadata checked WorldCat392066.
